subject: Provider bakeoff: guardrails, throttle behavior, and test owners
messages:
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@aegishealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + data & SLA asks

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the demo was helpful. A few follow-ups from our engineering and procurement teams so we can finish internally: 

- Can you share concrete uptime numbers you’ve observed in production (p95/p99 latencies and an SLO target) and how you compare to the major hyperscalers (AWS/Google) under sustained load?
- What are Redwood-hosted API rate limits and throttling behavior? For example, token/sec and request/sec defaults, burst behavior, and how you handle backpressure when a tenant exceeds quota (retry headers, 429 semantics, queueing).
- How does failover look if a region or availability zone becomes degraded? Does traffic automatically fall through to another model/region and what is the expected RTO/RPO?
- We also need a sample SLA clause and a simple table of what you provide on Dedicated vs Hosted for reliability and audit evidence.

If you can attach a short bakeoff plan and a test matrix we’ll share with our infra team. We’d like to run a comparative exercise vs AWS Bedrock and Vertex if possible.

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (stub)

Emily (procurement) will be looped in on the next thread for SLA language.

Appreciate it — Emma
Emma Liao
Senior PM, Platform
AegisHealth
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + data & SLA asks

Hi Emma — great to meet you today. Short recap and proposed next steps below. I’ve attached a concise bakeoff plan and an SLO summary to make it easier for your infra and procurement teams.

Key Redwood differentiators (quick):
- Predictable serving with dedicated pools (Reserved) and transparent fallback policies to lower-cost hosted variants when capacity is constrained.
- Cache-aware routing and KV prefix caching that reduces per-token cost and improves p95 under sustained sessions.
- Explicit failover policies: primary region, warm standby region, and automatic model variant fallback with observable handoff events in the Console.

What I’m proposing for the bakeoff (owners & timing):
1) Sustained QPS and latency histograms (owner: karthik_iyer) — 48-hour test at target QPS, collect p50/p95/p99, tail latency, and cold-start behaviors across model variants.
2) Throttle & burst behavior (owner: ben_carter) — ramp tests that exceed per-tenant quota to observe 429s, retry headers, token-based throttles, and whether responses are queue-delayed vs immediate rejection.
3) Failover simulation (owner: karthik_iyer) — simulate AZ/region outage and measure RTO (time to failover) and request loss; test both Hosted API and Dedicated fallback path.
4) Error-budget and degradation policy review (owner: grace_oconnor) — align on SLO thresholds and acceptable mitigation (graceful degradation, partial responses, or offline mode).

Deliverables and timing: bakeoff-plan-v1.xlsx (attached), SLO summary PDF (attached). Proposal: kickoff next Monday 2027-05-17, run tests through 2027-05-18, share results by 2027-05-20.

Links: A short shared Drive doc with the test harness and scripts is here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AegisBakeoffPlan. I also created a HubSpot task under deal AH-2027-06-RDWD-01 so both sides can track progress.

Questions/asks from your side: please confirm the list of regions you want included in the failover test and whether we have API keys for any Dedicated endpoints.

Attachments: bakeoff-plan-v1.xlsx, slo-summary.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally to lock owners and resource needs.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Liao <emma.liao@aegishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + data & SLA asks

Adding technical detail for the test plan. Quoting Grace: 

> 1) Sustained QPS and latency histograms (owner: karthik_iyer) — 48-hour test at target QPS, collect p50/p95/p99, tail latency, and cold-start behaviors across model variants.

Plan notes:
- Test harness: we’ll use wrk-llm (our internal fork) to drive a mix of short-prompt and long-context sessions. We’ll run variants: quantized (int8), fp16, and a smaller encoder-only model to compare baseline hyperscaler offering.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency for token streaming and non-streaming; 99.99th-percentile error rate; memory/KV cache hit ratio; per-request token cost estimate.
- SLA baseline to compare: we typically offer a 99.95% uptime SLA for Dedicated pools and best-effort Hosted with documented rate limits. For bakeoff, we’ll instrument synthetic errors to map to an error budget of 0.05% over 30 days.
- Failover behavior: our route table will try primary -> warm-standby region -> hosted-variant fallback. Expected RTO observed in previous runs is ~30–90s depending on session type; we’ll capture exact handoff traces in the Console.

Resource/ops asks:
- Need infra to allocate a small Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) for isolated runs and a Hosted account with default quotas for comparison.
- Ben: please schedule throttle experiments (see details below).

I’ll own the resilience harness and logging/tracing. I’ll post exact wrk-llm commands in the Drive doc by EOD.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Liao <emma.liao@aegishealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provider bakeoff: guardrails, throttle behavior, and test owners

I’ll take the throttle & burst experiments. Plan outline: 
- Baseline: record default Hosted API limits for a fresh tenant (requests/sec, tokens/sec) and document the 429 behavior and Retry-After header semantics.
- Ramp test: 0 -> 200% of quota over 10 minutes, hold for 30 minutes, then 500% burst for 1 minute to observe queueing and token-based throttles.
- Observables: count of 429s, presence/value of Retry-After, latency distribution before and after throttling, and whether errors are deterministic or per-call.
- Script: throttle-scripts.sh (attached stub) – will also produce a CSV of per-second error rate and average tokens/sec.

Infra ask: need temporary increase of Hosted quota for the AegisHealth test account to avoid soft-blocks during the ramp. Grace — can you confirm we have a test key and ITP for the tenant? Emma — if you can provision or confirm credentials, I’ll schedule the runs 2027-05-17 morning as proposed.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
